findings.passage: Anybody in college can read that affidavit and sign it and vote. So there is absolutely, positively no impediment to voting with a student ID as a secondary ID.
findings.note: Quoted by the Associated Press (story carried by LEX 18) in the Senate debate on SB 80, which removed college ID from the primary voter-ID list but kept it as a secondary ID with a signed affidavit. The story says the vote was on a Tuesday and was published 2024-01-31; WEKU dates the Senate vote 2024-01-30. The two sentences are printed in the story as two quotes joined by 'Sen. Gex Williams said'.

findings.passage: People should be able to vote without photo identification. Strongly Disagree
findings.note: His ticked answer on the iVoterGuide questionnaire, 'Elections and Voting' section, for the 2022 general election (the same answer appears on the 2022 primary page, election/885). The statement is 'People should be able to vote without photo identification.' and his answer is 'Strongly Disagree'. Date is the election date the page lists, not the date he answered.

findings.passage: Strengthen procedures to ensure only qualified voters are registered on the voter roles, better ensure the authenticity and chain of custody of absentee ballots and ensure voting machine source code is transparent. Results should be verifiable via audits prior to certification.
findings.note: His written answer to 'What laws would you propose to change present voting practices?' on the same 2022 iVoterGuide questionnaire. Date is the election date the page lists, not the date he answered.
